title: LambyOS Setup

balloons.text: Hi! It looks like you're restoring a session. Want a hand?
Want to know what this place is?
You'll be restoring someone's session. Three of them, actually!
Things sound better with headphones! Want a test sound?
You won't need to walk. Just turn!
One more thing before we start.
Before we begin, let me show you what we do!

about.title: About this project
paragraphs: This is a piece about how organised “conversion” networks (SOGICE) targeted queer people online, from 1997 to 2026. Four updates, thirty years: none of them changed who anyone was.

It is part of SurvivingSOGICE, a research project at the University of Bergen's Center for Digital Narrative. Everything in it rests on that research: at the end you will find a Library with the Lexicon — the words these networks used and the reasons they gave — and the full list of sources is in the menu, under Credits & attributions.
It was directed by the project, and written and built in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).

note.title: CONTENT NOTE
note.body: This depicts how organised “conversion” networks target queer people online — in their own tactics and language. It has brief flashing when a system fails, and a few moments when the view is moved for you between rooms (with Reduce motion, those become cuts). You can leave at any time; nothing you do is kept.
note.menu: Esc — or the corner button — opens the menu: pause, where you are, controls, credits, leave.

session.title: Whose session?
session.body: On this one machine: three people's sessions, four updates, thirty years of care. Their user profiles are still pending: you fill them in as you go, and the programme keeps what you give it.
